fishplate.context: Two rail ends meeting with a long plate bolted across the joint. Used for rail joint, track construction and permanent way maintenance topics.

railroad-tie.context: A wooden sleeper with a rail standing on each end. Used for track building, rail infrastructure and sleeper replacement topics.

rail-spike.context: An upright iron spike with a flat hooked head and a pointed tip. Used for track fastening, rail construction and old fashioned railroading.

rail-fastening-clip.context: A rail foot profile held down on a sleeper by a spring clip on each side. Used for track fixing, rail fastening systems and engineering diagrams.

tie-plate.context: A flat steel plate seen from above with a rail seat in the middle and four square spike holes. Used for track components and permanent way supplies.

track-ballast.context: A railway track cross section showing two rails on a sleeper above a mound of stones. Used for track bed, ballast and civil engineering topics.

check-rail.context: A curved running rail with a short guard rail alongside its inner edge, tied with spacer blocks. Used for sharp curves and derailment protection topics.

turnout-frog.context: A V shaped crossing nose where two rails meet with wing rails on both sides. Used for points, switches and track layout topics.

switch-point-blade.context: A tapered movable rail tongue beside a straight rail with an arrow showing it swing across. Used for points operation and switch maintenance.

diamond-crossing.context: Two tracks crossing each other at a shallow angle so the rails form a diamond. Used for junctions and track layout diagrams.

scissors-crossover.context: Two parallel tracks joined by two diagonal links that cross in the middle. Used for track layout and station throat diagrams.

three-way-switch.context: A single track splitting into left, straight and right tracks from one point. Used for yard layouts and triple points.

derailer.context: A wedge shaped block clamped on a rail beside a post with a flag sign. Used for siding safety and yard protection.

rail-expansion-joint.context: Two rail ends cut diagonally and overlapping side by side so they can slide with heat. Used for bridges and long welded rail topics.

third-rail.context: A track cross section with two running rails and a covered power rail beside them. Used for electric traction and metro power systems.

catenary-tensioner.context: A mast with a pulley wheel and a stack of weights hanging from a cable. Used for overhead wire tension and electrification topics.

track-gauge.context: Two rails with a horizontal arrow measuring the distance between their inner edges. Used for gauge standards and track measurement.

dual-gauge-track.context: Three rails on shared sleepers carrying both a narrow and a wide gauge. Used for mixed gauge lines and gauge changeover areas.

point-motor.context: A trackside box with a rod driving a switch blade. Used for remote controlled points and signalling equipment.

switch-stand.context: A ground lever beside the track with a post topped by a round target disc. Used for manual points and yard switching.

balise.context: A flat beacon box fixed between the two rails on the track. Used for train control, automatic protection and positioning.

axle-counter.context: A rail with a small sensor clamped under the head and a wheel passing above. Used for train detection and signalling.

track-circuit.context: Two rails joined by a battery at one end and a relay at the other. Used for train detection and signalling diagrams.

trackside-cabinet.context: A tall double door equipment cabinet with vents and a cable running into the ground. Used for signalling and telecom equipment by the line.

railway-milepost.context: A short post with a slanted face showing a number beside the track. Used for distance markers and location references.

gradient-post.context: A trackside post with one arm sloping up and one sloping down. Used for slope and grade markers.

speed-restriction-board.context: A trackside sign on a post showing a large number for a speed limit. Used for line speed and temporary restrictions.

whistle-post.context: A small trackside sign on a post marked with the letter W. Used for horn signs before crossings and tunnels.

station-name-board.context: A long sign held between two posts with a single line of text. Used for station names and platform signage.

platform-number-sign.context: A square sign with a large number hanging from a canopy on two rods. Used for platform numbers and station wayfinding.

island-platform.context: A long narrow platform seen from above with a track on each side and a canopy line down its middle. Used for station layout and boarding diagrams.

train-boarding-ramp.context: A ramp running from a platform edge up to a train door. Used for step free access and boarding assistance.

dispatch-paddle.context: A round signal disc on a short handle, held up to send a train off. Used for station staff and departure signals.

track-detonator.context: A small disc strapped on top of a rail with straps folded under the head. Used for emergency warning and fog signals.

crossing-bell.context: A round bell with sound arcs on a post above a crossed warning sign. Used for level crossing alarms.

gated-level-crossing.context: A road crossing the railway with a closed barrier on each side of the tracks. Used for level crossing safety and road rail interface.

pedestrian-level-crossing.context: A footpath crossing the rails with zigzag barriers at both sides. Used for pedestrian crossing and walkway safety around tracks.

dwarf-signal.context: A squat ground level signal box with two lamps in its face. Used for shunting and yard movement signals.

distant-signal.context: A semaphore post with a fishtail arm that has a V shaped notch in its end. Used for caution aspects and old style signals.

position-light-signal.context: A round signal target on a post with three lamps in a line. Used for position light and colour light signals.

route-indicator.context: A signal head with a diagonal row of lamps extending from its top corner. Used for junction route and diverging route displays.

banner-repeater-signal.context: A round signal window on a post with one dark bar across its centre. Used for repeating signal aspects and caution displays.

signal-gantry.context: An overhead frame spanning the tracks with signal heads hanging above lines. Used for multi track signalling and signal bridges.

cab-signal-display.context: A driver cab screen showing a speed dial beside a signal lamp. Used for in cab signalling and driver information.

signal-post-telephone.context: A signal post box with a telephone handset symbol on its door. Used for trackside phones and driver to signaller contact.

signaling-panel.context: A control panel with a track diagram of lines and switches above a row of buttons. Used for signal boxes and traffic control rooms.

single-line-token.context: A round metal token with a centre hole above a leather pouch. Used for single track working and train authority.

block-instrument.context: A wooden instrument box with a half dial and needle above a handle knob. Used for block signalling between signal boxes.

ground-frame.context: A small lever frame with three levers, one of them pulled over. Used for local points and signal control beside the line.

spike-maul.context: A long handled hammer with a slim double ended head. Used for driving spikes into sleepers.

rail-claw-bar.context: A long steel bar with a forked claw at one end. Used for pulling spikes out of sleepers.

rail-tongs.context: A pair of hinged tongs with curved jaws gripping a short length of rail. Used for carrying and lifting rail.

track-wrench.context: A very long open ended spanner. Used for tightening fishplate bolts and other track fittings.

track-jack.context: A squat jack with a toe plate under a rail and a ratchet handle on top. Used for lifting track to level or pack it.

rail-saw.context: A portable cutting saw with a round abrasive disc over a rail. Used for cutting rail to length.

rail-drill.context: A drilling machine clamped beside a rail with its bit pointing into the web. Used for making bolt holes in rail.

rail-bender.context: A heavy frame with a screw and handle bending a rail into a curve. Used for shaping rail on site.

tamping-pick.context: A track pick with one pointed end and one flat paddle end. Used for packing ballast under sleepers by hand.

ballast-fork.context: A wide fork with many long straight tines and a D shaped handle. Used for lifting stones without soil.

rail-thermometer.context: A round dial thermometer with a magnetic base stuck to a rail. Used for measuring rail temperature in hot weather.

thermite-welding.context: A crucible pouring a stream of molten metal into the gap between two rail ends. Used for joining rail by welding on site.

rerailing-ramp.context: A steel ramp on a rail with a wheel climbing up it. Used for putting derailed rolling stock back on the track.

track-trolley.context: A small flat trolley on rails with a push handle at one end. Used for moving tools and crews along the line.

rail-speeder.context: A small motorised rail car with a boxy cab and flanged wheels. Used for line inspection and light track work.

rail-flaw-detector.context: A walking trolley on one rail with a push handle and a screen showing a pulse trace. Used for finding cracks in rail.

track-geometry-car.context: A rail coach with a sensor beam under its middle sending laser lines down to the rails. Used for measuring track position and quality.

tamping-machine.context: A long track machine with a cab at each end and tines plunging into the ballast. Used for lining and packing track.

ballast-regulator.context: A short track vehicle with a plough blade at the front and a brush at the back. Used for shaping the stone bed beside the rails.

track-laying-machine.context: A gantry vehicle lowering a ready made panel of rails and sleepers onto the ground. Used for new track construction.

overhead-line-vehicle.context: A rail vehicle with a raised railed platform reaching an overhead wire. Used for catenary maintenance and electrification work.

rail-grinding-train.context: A rail vehicle with grinding stones under its body and sparks at the rail. Used for smoothing and reprofiling rails.

rail-pass.context: A folding booklet with a train front on its cover. Used for travel passes, rail cards and season tickets.

train-timetable.context: A printed sheet with a train front above a grid of departure times. Used for schedules, departures and journey planning.

quiet-carriage.context: A train carriage with a hushing face symbol, a finger held to the lips. Used for quiet coaches and silent travel zones.

first-class-carriage.context: A train carriage with a numeral 1 above its windows and a stripe along its body. Used for first class travel and premium seating.

reserved-seat-tag.context: A seat headrest with a small reservation card clipped on it. Used for seat reservations and booked seating.

train-seat.context: Two upholstered train seats side by side with tall backs and a shared armrest. Used for passenger seating and seat selection.
